newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil claims victory in fight for human rights.
newsitem.headline: Brazil claims victory in fight for human rights.

text.p: President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said on Tuesday Brazil was winning the fight for respect of human rights and the image of Latin America's largest country had improved dramatically abroad.

In a weekly radio address, Cardoso said the International Commission on Human Rights had withdrawn from its agenda the 1992 massacre by prison guards of 111 inmates at the Carandiru jail in Sao Paulo state.

"This month, Brazil is no longer in the dock out there. Brazil has won a vote of confidence," the sociology professor turned politician said. He said Brazil's new standing in the area of human rights was the result of a National Plan for Human Rights launched last May 13.

"The commission took its decision (over Carandiru) because we now have a policy of human rights," he said. The National Plan for Human Rights was intended to make rights abuses federal crimes, to punish torture, tackle police impunity and outlaw discrimination of any kind in the workplace or at home.

In addition to proposing specific laws, it aims to "promote a culture of human rights" through education to reduce violence, improve protection for children and enshrine Indian minority rights in law. Many of its elements have still to be voted into law by Congress.
